findings.text: a real changed path whose name opens with an absence word and a non-word character is read as a declaration, so a review run that changed such a file promotes with no commit and the ledger records no scope: at head `_changed_paths_declare_no_paths` returns True for `changed_paths: none.txt` while `_changed_paths_inside_repository` resolves the same field to ('none.txt',), and `_require_commit_for_changed_manifest` (reckon/crew/promotion.py:1819) short-circuits on it, where the same manifest at the dispatch base was refused with "has a complete manifest with changed_paths, but the manifest field 'commits' is missing. Promotion cannot verify changed repository paths without the commit that contains them"; both ends are measured end to end through crew.complete with a seeded repository file of that name — probe-absence-named-path.log prints PROMOTED_WITH_NO_COMMIT commits=[] at head and probe-absence-named-path-base.log prints REFUSED at base — and `_ABSENCE_BOUNDARY = r"(?!\w)"` over the vocabulary {"none", "n/a", "nil", "-"} means `none.txt`, `nil.rs` and `-x.csv` all qualify, while the delivered case that pins a kept path uses `candidate.txt`, which does not open with an absence word.

the head gate log's command line reads `command=... -m pytest -n 6 -p no:cacheprovider -q <files>`, the file list left as a placeholder rather than the 26 paths the arm measured; the `files=` line beneath it names all 26 and line 1 carries the correct revision and tree, so the result is corroborated while the command echo is not the command.
